rules.statement: A registrar of births, deaths, and marriages is not a public servant within the meaning of the Public Servants' (Liabilities) Ordinance, No. 2 of 1899.
rules.supporting_quote: "The respondent here urges he is 'a person employed in the service of the Government of the Colony '. In construing the word 'employed ', however, it is not always easy to see what test has to be applied. It has been held for instance that a person who works for a daily wage, such as a tide-waiter at the Customs, a railway department labourer or a public works labourer, although they are certainly employed in the service of the Government and are paid out of Government funds, are not public servants within the meaning of the Ordinance (Palaniappa Chetty v. Fernando 1[1 A. C R. 27.])."
